userStories.title: Catalog changes and a body slug source
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Re-scope code-intel keys to projects, make intake keys public, and let ProjectMembershipGuard resolve a body-sourced slug.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the legacy decorators, CASL factory and helpers, so every route has to be on keys first.

**Approach** — Catalog changes:
All in `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts` and the `catalog_scope` column of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv`, whose rows `catalog.spec.ts` re-reads:

| Key | Baseline | Target | Effect on the seeded roles (by `expandEntries`) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `codeintel.read` | inventory `global` (4 rows) | `project` (all 4 rows) | Held by every project role through `*.read`, and by Developer through `codeintel.*`. Today: global ADMIN only through the catalog; project ADMIN, DEVELOPER and every rostered agent through CASL. |
| `codeintel.index.write` | inventory `global` (1 row) | `project` | Held by Project Admin and Developer. Today: global ADMIN and DEVELOPER-role agents. |
| `ci.webhook.ingest` | inventory `project`; role key | inventory `public`; added to `PUBLIC_KEYS` | Public: access `public`, scope `any`, in no role. Project Admin's `*` no longer reaches it (a public key is not role-grantable). |
| `vcs.webhook.ingest` | inventory `project`; role key | inventory `public`; added to `PUBLIC_KEYS` | Same as `ci.webhook.ingest`. |

The catalog stays at 226 keys; the public key count goes from 7 to 9. Every other key in this feature is used as it is.

`ProjectMembershipGuard.resolveSlug` reads `req.params.slug` first, as today. Otherwise, for `source: 'query'` it reads `req.query[key]` (unchanged) and for `source: 'body'` it reads `req.body[key]` when `req.body` is an object. Either way a value that is not a non-empty string is no slug. Fastify parses the JSON body before guards run, so `req.body` is available.

`ProjectScopedRequest` (`apps/api/src/projects/project-context.ts`) gains `body?: unknown`. Preserve all legacy guard branches for routes not migrated by this feature. A body with no usable slug passes membership resolution without attaching context; RequiresGuard on the downstream project-key route fails closed rather than guessing a project.

**Interface** — `apps/api/src/projects/project-slug-from.decorator.ts` target:
```ts
export interface ProjectSlugSource { source: 'query' | 'body'; key: string; }
export const ProjectSlugFrom = (source: 'query' | 'body', key: string) =>
  SetMetadata<string, ProjectSlugSource>(PROJECT_SLUG_FROM_KEY, { source, key });
```

**Scope** — In: catalog and inventory scope cells; body metadata/request typing and slug resolution; update catalog.spec.ts PUBLIC_KEY_LIST to the existing seven plus both intake keys, preserving all other catalog derivations; unit behavior for catalog expansion, anonymous public-key bypass and slug resolution. Out: applying decorators to controllers (US-002 to US-006), OpenAPI export (US-006), new role entries, stored-role rewrites, cleanup of legacy authorization branches, and manual design-doc public-key list edits. The catalog scope and body metadata are the seams consumed by US-002, and public access is consumed by US-004/US-005.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `PUBLIC_KEY_LIST` holds the seven design public keys, and "exports the public, implicit and ownable key sets" asserts `PUBLIC_KEYS` equals it, while "derives access, scope, ownable, risk, principals and approval for every catalog key" derives `access` from the same list. The replacing invariant: `PUBLIC_KEY_LIST` holds those seven plus `ci.webhook.ingest` and `vcs.webhook.ingest`, and every other derivation (including `codeintel.read` and `codeintel.index.write` scoped `project` from the edited TSV rows) is unchanged.

userStories.title: Code-intel routes check keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce project-scoped permission keys on all five /code-intel routes and the project impact route.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the legacy decorators, CASL factory and helpers, so every route has to be on keys first.

**Approach** — Route keys (`G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key. Every project route has `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`):
| Route | Key | Guards | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /code-intel/index` | `codeintel.index.write` | project (slug from body `projectSlug`) | `@RequiredPermission([MANAGE, 'AstIndex'])` + controller `checkProjectMembership` |
| `GET /code-intel/symbols`, `…/symbols/:symbolId`, `…/:symbolId/callers`, `…/:symbolId/callees` | `codeintel.read` | project (slug from query `projectSlug`, unchanged) | `@ProjectPermission([READ, 'CodeIntel'])` |
| `GET /projects/:slug/codeintel/impact` | `codeintel.impact.read` | project | `@ProjectPermission([READ, 'CodeIntel'])` |

A route with a project key has `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)` in one call, both at the method level or both at the class level; never class-level `RequiresGuard` with method-level `ProjectMembershipGuard`.

Order of checks on every migrated route:
1. authentication (the global guards; skipped by `@Public()`);
2. project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 `projects` for a missing project, 403 `projects` for a principal with no access);
3. the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`);
4. input validation (the global `ValidationPipe`, then any handler-level parse);
5. lookups and domain rules in the handler and services (404s, 409s, the HMAC 401s).
The first failing step decides the response.

`POST /code-intel/index` and the four symbol reads with no `projectSlug` resolve no project: `ProjectMembershipGuard` passes, and `RequiresGuard` refuses the project key with 403 `permissions` (fail closed) before validation.

Constructors drop a dependency only when the removed checks were its last use: `CodeIntelController` and `ContextController` drop `ProjectAccessService` when they switch to `@CurrentProject()`; `ProjectSkillsController` drops `ProjectAccessService`. For this story change CodeIntelController only: remove resolveProject/checkProjectMembership, delegate indexing with ctx.project.id, and retain all read parsing, pagination, project isolation, JsonResponse.Ok and symbol lookup behavior. getChangeImpact retains its CurrentProject-based behavior and required-query 400, replacing only the legacy decoration/guard. ProjectMembershipGuard remains provided by the already imported ProjectAccessModule; PermissionsModule is global and RequiresGuard needs no provider entry. Refused keys throw new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions') with message permissions.403.

**Interface** — Target handler signature (parameters not listed are unchanged): `CodeIntelController.indexCommit(@Body() dto, @CurrentProject() ctx)`. The downstream call is `AstIndexService.indexCommit(repoId, commitHash, files, ctx.project.id)`. Index uses `@ProjectSlugFrom('body', 'projectSlug')`; reads retain `@ProjectSlugFrom('query', 'projectSlug')`.

**Scope** — In: CodeIntelController and ProjectsController.getChangeImpact; corresponding existing unit/search/metadata/project-role integration tests and binding-only HTTP ACs. Update code-intel.controller.spec.ts to supply PermissionService and use indexCommit(dto, ctx), removing handler-owned 404/nonmember tests; getSymbol/getCallers/getCallees cases remain unchanged. Update both modules in code-intel-search.controller.spec.ts with a codeintel.read-allowing PermissionService double or overridden RequiresGuard, preserving dispatch/search assertions. In test/integration/ast-index/code-intel-controller-permissions.integration.spec.ts assert REQUIRES_METADATA keys ['codeintel.index.write'] on indexCommit and ['codeintel.read'] on all four reads, undefined PERMISSION_KEY/PROJECT_PERMISSION_KEY on all five, and index body slug metadata. In test/integration/code-intel/code-intel-project-roles.integration.spec.ts let pviewer read all five reads, keep outsider refusal and missing/empty/repeated slug fail-closed cases, preserving admin/developer/agent/root behavior. In projects.controller.spec.ts replace the legacy impact metadata expectation with ['codeintel.impact.read'] and add it to the migrated project route table, preserving behavior assertions. Out: catalog/body resolver implementation (US-001), context/VCS/webhook/skills migrations (US-003 to US-006), final OpenAPI export (US-006), and deleting shared CASL/decorators/helpers (cleanup).

Integration fixtures seed system roles after resetDb or boot the app. Binding-only users have no ProjectMember or global admin role; binding-only agents have no AgentProject or AgentRoleEntry. A custom-role user holds only a custom PROJECT role with ['ticket.read'] in p1. Agent project scoping is on. Route allow/refuse tests use actual authorization, not an allowing guard double; doubles are for standalone controller harness wiring. No approval and no audit change: permitted requests run immediately. Only existing e2e cases a correct implementation breaks are edited.

The replacing invariant: both modules provide a `PermissionService` double that allows `codeintel.read` (or override `RequiresGuard`), and every dispatch and search assertion is unchanged.

its module provides no `PermissionService`, and its five metadata cases assert `PERMISSION_KEY` (MANAGE AstIndex) on `indexCommit` and `PROJECT_PERMISSION_KEY` (READ CodeIntel) on the four reads. The replacing invariant: `REQUIRES_METADATA` keys are `['codeintel.index.write']` on `indexCommit` and `['codeintel.read']` on `searchSymbols`, `getSymbol`, `getCallers` and `getCallees`; `PERMISSION_KEY` and `PROJECT_PERMISSION_KEY` are undefined on all five; `indexCommit`'s project slug source is `{ source: 'body', key: 'projectSlug' }`.

The replacing invariant: a project VIEWER gets 200 from the five read routes (Viewer holds `codeintel.read` and `codeintel.impact.read`); `outsider` still gets 403; the fail-closed missing, empty and repeated `projectSlug` cases still answer 403; the admin, developer, agent and root cases are unchanged.

its case "code-intel impact keeps the legacy @ProjectPermission until the integrations story moves it" asserts `PROJECT_PERMISSION_KEY` is defined and `REQUIRES_METADATA` is undefined on `getChangeImpact`. The replacing invariant: `getChangeImpact` carries `REQUIRES_METADATA` keys `['codeintel.impact.read']` and no `PROJECT_PERMISSION_KEY`, and joins the file's table of migrated project-scoped routes; the `getChangeImpact` behaviour cases are unchanged.

userStories.title: Context routes check keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace context CASL and in-handler membership checks with ordered project access and context permission keys.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the legacy decorators, CASL factory and helpers, so every route has to be on keys first.

**Approach** — Route keys (`G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key. Every project route has `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`):
| Route | Key | Guards | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /context/:slug` | `context.read` | project | `@RequiredPermission([READ, 'ProjectContext'])` + controller `checkProjectMembership` |
| `POST /context/:slug/query` | `context.query` | project | same |

A route with a project key has `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)` in one call, both at the method level or both at the class level; never class-level `RequiresGuard` with method-level `ProjectMembershipGuard`.

Order of checks on every migrated route:
1. authentication (the global guards; skipped by `@Public()`);
2. project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 `projects` for a missing project, 403 `projects` for a principal with no access);
3. the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`);
4. input validation (the global `ValidationPipe`, then any handler-level parse);
5. lookups and domain rules in the handler and services (404s, 409s, the HMAC 401s).
The first failing step decides the response.

**Seeded roles stay as Appendix A.** In particular `context.query` is held only by Project Admin and Developer, so a Viewer keeps `GET /context/:slug` but loses `POST /context/:slug/query`. An admin who wants otherwise edits the Viewer role.

Constructors drop a dependency only when the removed checks were its last use: `CodeIntelController` and `ContextController` drop `ProjectAccessService` when they switch to `@CurrentProject()`; `ProjectSkillsController` drops `ProjectAccessService`. This story changes ContextController only: remove resolveProjectId/checkProjectMembership and the null-principal refusal, use the guarded context project id and principal.id, and keep buildQuery/parseQuery, defaults, optional fields and response envelope unchanged. PermissionsModule is global; RequiresGuard needs no provider entry; ContextModule already imports ProjectAccessModule. A refused key answers 403 `new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')` with message `permissions.403`; project guard responses and domain behavior are unchanged.

**Interface** — Target handler signatures (parameters not listed are unchanged): `ContextController.getContext(@Query() queryDto, @Principal() principal, @CurrentProject() ctx)` and `queryContext(@Body() body, @Principal() principal, @CurrentProject() ctx)`. Both call ContextBuilderService.getProjectContext using projectId ctx.project.id and actorId principal.id with the same parsed fields as before.

**Scope** — In: ContextController and its existing direct-call unit spec plus binding-only HTTP integration ACs. context.controller.spec.ts supplies a PermissionService double and uses getContext(dto, principal, ctx)/queryContext(body, principal, ctx); remove direct-call slug-resolution, missing/soft-deleted project, nonmember and null-principal checks because the guards own them and HTTP ACs pin those outcomes. Preserve query-building and response assertions. Out: catalog/body-slug changes (US-001), code-intel/VCS/webhook/skills routes (US-002 and US-004 to US-006), final OpenAPI export (US-006), shared CASL/helper deletion, role-entry changes and approval/audit behavior.

Integration fixtures seed system roles after resetDb or boot the app. Binding-only users have a p1 RoleBinding but no ProjectMember or global admin role; binding-only agents have no AgentProject or AgentRoleEntry. A custom-role user holds only a custom PROJECT role with ['ticket.read']; no-access users have no binding, membership or global admin role touching p1. Agent project scoping is on. Use actual route authorization for integration cases; provider doubles only isolate standalone unit harnesses. Only existing e2e cases a correct implementation breaks are edited.

The replacing invariant: the module provides a `PermissionService` double; `getContext(dto, principal, ctx)` and `queryContext(body, principal, ctx)` call `ContextBuilderService.getProjectContext` with `projectId` `ctx.project.id` and `actorId` `principal.id` and the same parsed query fields as before; the slug, 404, non-member and null-principal cases are removed because the guards own them (pinned at HTTP by US-003 ACs 5 to 8); the query-building and response assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: VCS routes check keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Authorize all nine VCS management routes by project keys and declare the public VCS intake key without changing HMAC processing.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the legacy decorators, CASL factory and helpers, so every route has to be on keys first.

**Approach** — Route keys (`G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key. Every project route has `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`):
| Route | Key | Guards | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.create` | project | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` + `assertProjectMembership` |
| `GET /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.read` | project | same |
| `PATCH /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.update` | project | same |
| `DELETE /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.delete` | project | same |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/test` | `vcs.connection.test` | project | same |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate` | `vcs.webhook-secret.rotate` | project | `@ProjectRoles('ADMIN')` + `isUserPrincipal` refusal |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/sync/:issueNumber` | `vcs.sync.issue` | project | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` + `assertProjectMembership` |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/sync` | `vcs.sync.all` | project | same |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/sync-pr` | `vcs.sync.pr` | project | same |
| `POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook` | `vcs.webhook.ingest` | public (`@Public()` kept) | none (HMAC in controller, unchanged) |

`VcsController` gains class-level `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)`, and the rotate route's method-level `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard)` is removed (ruling 3).

A route with a project key has `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)` in one call, both at the method level or both at the class level; never class-level `RequiresGuard` with method-level `ProjectMembershipGuard`. A global route (no project) has `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` only. A public route keeps `@Public()` and adds `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, the pattern in `apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts`.

Order of checks on every migrated route:
1. authentication (the global guards; skipped by `@Public()`);
2. project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 `projects` for a missing project, 403 `projects` for a principal with no access);
3. the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`);
4. input validation (the global `ValidationPipe`, then any handler-level parse);
5. lookups and domain rules in the handler and services (404s, 409s, the HMAC 401s).
The first failing step decides the response.

**Who may act is role data, not code.** The user-only refusals on `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate`, the three project-skills routes and `SkillsService.createSource` are removed. An agent rotates a secret or enables a skill only if an admin bound it to a role holding the key. Whether an agent's high-risk write must wait for approval is approval policy, delivered in P3; this feature adds no approval step. In this story remove only the VCS refusal.

**The intake routes declare public keys.** `ci.webhook.ingest` and `vcs.webhook.ingest` join `PUBLIC_KEYS`. The routes keep `@Public()` and their HMAC signature check; a public key needs no principal, like the token-gated `invite.accept`. US-001 supplies public catalog classification; this story declares vcs.webhook.ingest on the intake handler, with RequiresGuard only and no project membership guard.

A handler that loads its project through `ProjectsService.findBySlug`, `WebhookService.getProjectBySlug` or `ProjectAccessService.findProjectIdBySlug` may keep that lookup or switch to `@CurrentProject()`; both resolve the same project after the guard. What is removed is every membership, admin or principal-type check the guards now cover. `VcsController` keeps `ProjectsService` (`findBySlug` still loads the full project, whose `key` the sync routes need). `VcsModule` already reaches ProjectAccessModule through ProjectsModule. PermissionsModule is global; RequiresGuard needs no provider entry.

Key refusals answer 403 `new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')` with message permissions.403. Unchanged: ProjectMembershipGuard's 404 and 403 projects, the handlers' 404s and 409s, the VCS 400 for a missing encryption key, and the intake routes' 401s. Keep decrypted-token/provider/sync behavior unchanged. `VcsConnectionResponseDto` carries `webhookSecretConfigured: boolean`, never the token or secret; Viewer read access must not expose a secret. Public intake keeps raw-byte signature verification, unknown-target/signature 401s, replay checks and ignored-connection behavior unchanged.

**Interface** — Target handler signature (parameters not listed are unchanged): `VcsController.rotateWebhookSecret(@CurrentProject() ctx)`. A VCS or webhook handler whose `@Principal()` parameter becomes unused once `assertProjectMembership` is removed drops it, and the unit specs that call it directly drop that argument too. Rotate delegates to VcsConnectionService.rotateWebhookSecret(ctx.project.id) without an actor-type check.

**Scope** — In: VcsController, VcsWebhookController, standalone test-module permission doubles and direct-call signature changes, plus role-binding HTTP cases. In vcs.controller.spec.ts remove/invert the eight assertProjectMembership-called and eight nonmember-refusal cases; replace the agent rotate refusal with context-only service delegation. Preserve 409, ValidationAppException and not-found cases. Provide PermissionService doubles in test/integration/vcs/vcs-controller.spec.ts, vcs-manual-sync.spec.ts, src/vcs/vcs-webhook.controller.spec.ts, test/integration/vcs/vcs-webhook.integration.spec.ts and vcs-webhook-pull-request.integration.spec.ts, preserving all delegation/sync/signature/replay/ignore/delivery/pull-request assertions. Out: public catalog edits (US-001), other route migrations (US-002, US-003, US-005, US-006), final OpenAPI export (US-006), changes to HMAC/replay/payload validation, approval, actor context/audit, and deleting shared legacy authorization infrastructure.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Authorize outbound webhook management by permission keys and declare public CI intake without changing its signature-gated behavior.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-cleanup` deletes the legacy decorators, CASL factory and helpers, so every route has to be on keys first.

**Approach** — Route keys (`G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key. Every project route has `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`):
| Route | Key | Guards | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /projects/:slug/webhooks` | `webhook.create` | project | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /projects/:slug/webhooks` | `webhook.read` | project | same |
| `PATCH /projects/:slug/webhooks/:id` | `webhook.update` | project | same |
| `DELETE /projects/:slug/webhooks/:id` | `webhook.delete` | project | same |
| `DELETE /webhooks/:id` | `webhook.delete` | global (`RequiresGuard` only, no project) | same |
| `POST /projects/:slug/ci-webhook` | `ci.webhook.ingest` | public (`@Public()` kept) | none (HMAC in controller, unchanged) |

A route with a project key has `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)` in one call, both at the method level or both at the class level; never class-level `RequiresGuard` with method-level `ProjectMembershipGuard`. A global route (no project) has `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` only. A public route keeps `@Public()` and adds `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, the pattern in `apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts`. Use method-level guard pairs on the project webhook routes so the global deletion has no project guard.

Order of checks on every migrated route:
1. authentication (the global guards; skipped by `@Public()`);
2. project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 `projects` for a missing project, 403 `projects` for a principal with no access);
3. the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`);
4. input validation (the global `ValidationPipe`, then any handler-level parse);
5. lookups and domain rules in the handler and services (404s, 409s, the HMAC 401s).
The first failing step decides the response.

`DELETE /webhooks/:id` resolves no project, so `RequiresGuard` asks `can` with no `projectId` for the `any`-scope `webhook.delete`; only a principal holding it globally (Owner, Admin, a legacy global ADMIN) passes. A Project Admin uses the project-scoped route.

A handler that loads its project through `ProjectsService.findBySlug`, `WebhookService.getProjectBySlug` or `ProjectAccessService.findProjectIdBySlug` may keep that lookup or switch to `@CurrentProject()`; both resolve the same project after the guard. What is removed is every membership, admin or principal-type check the guards now cover. Keep webhook ownership-scoped lookups and cross-project 404s. Viewer list access exposes no secret: `PrismaWebhookRepository.findByProject` selects `id`, `projectId`, `url`, `events` and `createdAt` only.

**Module wiring.** `ProjectMembershipGuard` is provided by `ProjectAccessModule`. `WebhookModule` (`apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.module.ts`) gains `ProjectAccessModule` in its imports; `VcsModule` already reaches it through `ProjectsModule`, and `CodeIntelModule`, `ContextModule` and `SkillsModule` already import it. PermissionsModule is global and RequiresGuard needs no provider entry.

**The intake routes declare public keys.** `ci.webhook.ingest` and `vcs.webhook.ingest` join `PUBLIC_KEYS`. The routes keep `@Public()` and their HMAC signature check; a public key needs no principal, like the token-gated `invite.accept`. Catalog classification is supplied by US-001; this story adds only the public declaration/RequiresGuard on CI intake. No ProjectMembershipGuard is added there. Preserve signedBytesOf, timing-safe signature checking, signature-before-payload-validation, replay handling, unknown-target 401 anti-enumeration and ticket creation. Key refusals answer 403 new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')/permissions.403; project guard 404/403 and domain 400/404/409/intake 401 behavior stay unchanged.

**Interface** — Use existing `WebhookService.getProjectBySlug` and `removeForProject` interfaces unchanged; `PermissionService.can(principal, key, { projectId? })` is reached through RequiresGuard. Global deletion supplies no projectId, unlike the project deletion route. Existing handler parameters stay unchanged unless switching to CurrentProject.

**Scope** — In: WebhookController, WebhookModule imports, CiWebhookController decoration, key-aware route harness and binding-only HTTP ACs. In webhook-routes.spec.ts replace the legacy ADMIN-gate harness/header with ProjectMembershipGuard dependencies or override plus a PermissionService double whose can refuses webhook.* for member and allows admin; denied keys return 403 without writes while existing 400, 404 and 201 cases remain unchanged. In ci-webhook.controller.spec.ts supply a PermissionService double and preserve existing 401, replay 409 and payload 400 assertions. Out: public catalog/body source edits (US-001), code-intel/context/VCS/skills migrations (US-002, US-003, US-004, US-006), final OpenAPI export (US-006), changes to HMAC/replay/payload processing, creator/audit additions to CI tickets, approval and deleting shared legacy authorization infrastructure.

Agent project scoping is on. Use real key evaluation for integration cases, not the unit harness's permission double. The class `ProjectSkillsController` keeps its class-level guard and becomes `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)`. A route with a project key has `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)` in one call, both at the method level or both at the class level; never class-level `RequiresGuard` with method-level `ProjectMembershipGuard`. A global route (no project) has `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` only.

Order of checks on every migrated route:

2. project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 `projects` for a missing project, 403 `projects` for a principal with no access);
3. the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`);
4. input validation (the global `ValidationPipe`, then any handler-level parse);
5. lookups and domain rules in the handler and services (404s, 409s, the HMAC 401s).
The first failing step decides the response.

**Who may act is role data, not code.** The user-only refusals on `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate`, the three project-skills routes and `SkillsService.createSource` are removed. An agent rotates a secret or enables a skill only if an admin bound it to a role holding the key. Whether an agent's high-risk write must wait for approval is approval policy, delivered in P3; this feature adds no approval step. This story removes the skills refusals only; VCS was migrated by US-004.

`PUT /projects/:slug/skills/:skillId` records the caller's id in `ProjectSkill.enabledById`, a plain nullable string with no foreign key, so an agent caller's id is stored as is. `POST /admin/skills/sources` records it in `SkillSource.createdById` the same way.

This story changes ProjectSkillsController only: remove assertUser/assertProjectMembership/assertProjectAdmin and its access dependency, keep caller id for enable, and drop unused principal parameters/imports from other handlers. Remove SkillsService.createSource's actor-type refusal only; preserve GitHub URL parsing, resolver behavior, uniqueness checks, transactional creation and all domain 404/409 responses. Global sources use skill.source.* keys held by global Owner/Admin; project roles do not gain them. Project read keys reach all project roles; enable/disable are held by Project Admin. PermissionsModule is global; RequiresGuard needs no provider entry; SkillsModule already imports ProjectAccessModule. Refused keys use new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions')/permissions.403, replacing skills.principal/skills.projectPrincipal or legacy admin refusals; project access errors remain projects.

`openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec` in the last story.
